about.title: Sonora Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Sonora's mix of rural properties, small-business storefronts along S Washington Street, and daily commutes on Rt 49 and Mono Way mean residents rely on all kinds of consumer, industrial, and household products every day — from farm equipment to power tools to vehicle parts. When one of those products fails because of a defect in its design, manufacturing, or warning label, the resulting injury can upend a family's routine fast. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim in these situations, meaning the focus is on the product's condition rather than proving anyone was careless. We help Sonora residents investigate defective product claims, identify every business in the supply chain that may share responsibility, and move the case forward — all while you focus on recovering.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective product cases, we can focus on proving the defect and the harm it caused, rather than digging into the manufacturer's state of mind.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law, so we evaluate every link in the chain that put the product in your hands.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Product
items.desc: Since the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence, our team can advise you early on how to keep it safe and intact for the claims process.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law often allows claims based on strict liability, which generally means you need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that the company was careless. We can explain which theory fits your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including packaging, instructions, and any parts that broke or malfunctioned. Don't attempt repairs or throw anything away. Preserving the product can be critical evidence for your claim.

items.question: Is this only for injuries that happen at home?
items.answer: No. Sonora residents get hurt by defective products in all kinds of settings — on job sites near Sanguinetti Road, in vehicles traveling Mono Way or Rt 49, or using tools and equipment around town. Wherever the incident happened, we can help you pursue a claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to contact us?
items.answer: No. There's no cost for an initial case review. We typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
